method: Build the fixture with scripts/benchmark_book.py helpers, render with the production LaTeX renderer, and compile each variant in three fresh temporary directories through the production _compile_latex helper. Inspect structure with pdfinfo -struct, named destinations with pdfinfo -dests, external URL annotations with pdfinfo -url, and text with pdftotext -layout.

paragraph_tagging_diagnostic.name: direct-paragraph-tagging-disabled
paragraph_tagging_diagnostic.fixture: Same branching N=10 fixture; three fresh temporary directories
paragraph_tagging_diagnostic.method: Insert \tagpdfsetup{para/tagging=false} directly before \begin{document} in the rendered source; compile with the production _compile_latex helper. This is a diagnostic-only change.
paragraph_tagging_diagnostic.conclusion: The median is 0.304 s (1.55%) slower than the current tagged baseline, with only 150 fewer bytes. Poppler reports Tagged: no, so this is not a viable production optimization.

interpretation.conclusion: Disabling structure destinations retained the inspected structure and links and reduced file size, but produced no meaningful compile-time improvement on this small fixture. This does not confirm the proposed PDF performance budget or predict larger books.
